messages.content: What is a variable?

A variable is a named box that holds a value. In JavaScript you create one with let, const, or var, then read or change the value by its name. `let score = 0;` makes a box called score holding 0, and `score = score + 1;` puts 1 in it.
What is a function?

A function is a reusable block of code with a name. You give it inputs called parameters, and it returns an output. `function add(a, b) { return a + b; }` defines it, and `add(2, 3)` calls it and gives back 5. Functions stop you writing the same code twice.
What is a loop?

A loop repeats code until a condition stops it. A for loop counts: `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { console.log(i); }` prints 0, 1, 2. A while loop repeats while a test is true. Use a loop whenever you would otherwise copy the same line many times.
What is an array?

An array is an ordered list of values in one variable. `let scores = [10, 20, 30];` holds three numbers. You read them by index starting at 0, so `scores[0]` is 10, and `scores.length` is 3. Methods like push, pop, and map change or transform the list.
What is the difference between let and var?

Both declare variables, but let is block scoped and var is function scoped. A variable declared with let inside an if block does not exist outside it, while var leaks out. let also forbids redeclaring the same name. Modern code uses let and const, and avoids var.
What is the difference between let and const?

let allows reassignment, const does not. `let score = 1; score = 2;` is fine, but `const score = 1; score = 2;` throws an error. const only locks the binding, not the contents, so a const array can still have items pushed into it. Use const by default and let only when you must reassign.
What is a promise?

A promise represents a value that will arrive later, such as data from a network request. It is either pending, fulfilled, or rejected. You wait for it with await inside an async function: `const data = await fetch(url);`. Errors are caught with try and catch. A promise avoids blocking the page while it waits.
What is the DOM?

The DOM is the browser's live tree of the page. Every element becomes a node in that tree, and JavaScript can read or change it. `document.querySelector('#score')` finds a node and `.textContent = '10'` changes what it shows. Changing the DOM is how JavaScript updates the screen.
What is an event listener?

An event listener runs a function when something happens, like a click or a key press. `button.addEventListener('click', () => { score++; });` runs the arrow function on every click. The browser calls it for you, which is why games react without polling in a loop.
How does a browser render a page?

The browser downloads the HTML, parses it into the DOM, and parses CSS into style rules. It then computes which styles apply to each node, lays out where every box goes, and paints the pixels. JavaScript can change the DOM after that, which forces a fresh layout and paint.
How does CSS layout work?

CSS lays out boxes inside boxes. display picks the layout mode: block stacks elements vertically, inline flows them with text, flex aligns children in a row or column, and grid places them in rows and columns. Properties such as gap, justify-content, and align-items control spacing and alignment inside them.
How do I centre a box with CSS?

Use flexbox on the parent: `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;` centres the child both ways. For a fixed-size box you can also use `margin: 0 auto;` to centre it horizontally, or `position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);` to centre it on top of other content.
Why is my canvas blank?

Check four things in order. First, the canvas has a real width and height, because a zero-sized canvas draws nothing. Second, you called getContext('2d') and saved the result. Third, you actually call fillRect or stroke after setting fillStyle. Fourth, nothing covers the canvas or draws in a colour matching the background.
Why does my code say undefined is not a function?

You are calling something that is not a function. Usually the method name is misspelled, or the value is undefined because querySelector found nothing. Log the object first: `console.log(button);`. If it prints null, the element was not on the page yet, so move the script to the end of the body or wait for DOMContentLoaded.
How do I fix a CORS error?

CORS is enforced by the browser, not by your code. The server must send an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for your page's origin. If you cannot change the server, request the data through your own backend and let it call the API, or use a public API that already allows cross-origin requests.

Teach me how to code

Start with one language and one project, not with theory. Use JavaScript because it runs in any browser with no install. Learn four things in this order: variables hold values, functions group steps, loops repeat steps, and conditions choose between steps. Then build a page that adds two numbers typed into boxes, and make it work before you read anything else.
Teach me JavaScript step by step

Step 1: open a browser console and type 2 + 2. Step 2: store it with `let x = 2 + 2;`. Step 3: group steps into `function add(a, b) { return a + b; }`. Step 4: repeat with `for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) console.log(i);`. Step 5: choose with `if (x > 3) { ... }`. Step 6: put those in an HTML file inside a script tag and open it. That is the whole core of the language.
Explain variables to a beginner

A variable is a label on a box. `let age = 12;` puts 12 in a box labelled age. Anywhere you write age, JavaScript looks inside the box and finds 12. Later `age = 13;` swaps the contents. The label stays the same, which is why you can reuse it.
Give me a lesson on loops

A loop repeats work. Count with a for loop: `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { console.log('lap ' + i); }` runs three times and prints lap 0, lap 1, lap 2. Repeat while a condition holds with `while (energy > 0) { energy--; }`. Walk a list with `for (const item of list) { console.log(item); }`. If you catch yourself copying a line, write a loop instead.
What should I build first?

Build a to-do list in one HTML file. It needs an input, a button, and a list element. The button reads the input, creates a list item, and appends it. That small project uses variables, functions, arrays, events, and the DOM all at once, so finishing it teaches more than three tutorials.

Explain what CSS does

CSS decides how HTML looks. HTML says what is on the page, and CSS says how big it is, what colour it is, and where it sits. A rule has a selector and declarations: `.card { padding: 16px; border-radius: 8px; }` styles every element with class card. Without CSS a page is plain black text on white.
Explain what JavaScript does

JavaScript makes the page react. HTML is structure and CSS is style, but both are fixed once loaded. JavaScript runs code in response to clicks, typing, and timers, and it can rewrite the page while it is open. That is what turns a document into a game or an app.
Explain what HTML does

HTML gives the page its structure. Each tag is a piece of content with a meaning: h1 is a heading, p is a paragraph, button is a clickable control, canvas is a drawing surface. The browser reads the tags and builds the DOM from them. Without HTML there is nothing for CSS to style or JavaScript to move.
